stem_html:
\(7(x-3)=4x+9\)

What is the solution to the given equation?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Distribute over both terms. \(7(x-3)\) is \(7x-21\), not \(7x-3\).
  • Move the variable to one side first.
  • Check by substituting. \(7(7)=49\) and \(4(10)+9=49\).

Why A is wrong 4 comes from \(7x-3=4x+9\), which drops the distribution over the second term of \(x-3\).

Why B is wrong −10 comes from subtracting the 9 instead of adding the 21: \(3x=-21-9=-30\).

Why C is wrong −4 comes from moving the 21 to the wrong side: \(3x=9-21=-12\).

Why D is right Expanding gives \(7x-21=4x+9\). Subtracting \(4x\) gives \(3x-21=9\), and adding 21 gives \(3x=30\), so \(x=10\).

stem_html: A candle burns at a constant rate. After 2 hours it is 24 centimetres tall, and after 5 hours it is 16.5 centimetres tall. The candle burns out when its height reaches 0. How many hours after it is lit does the candle burn out?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Neither given height is the starting height. Work back to \(t=0\).
  • The rate is a slope, not an answer.
  • Burning out is \(h(t)=0\), not \(t=0\).

Why A is right The rate is \(\dfrac{24-16.5}{5-2}=\dfrac{7.5}{3}=2.5\) centimetres per hour. The starting height is \(24+2(2.5)=29\), so \(h(t)=29-2.5t\) and the height is 0 when \(t=\dfrac{29}{2.5}=11.6\).

Why B is wrong This divides 24 by 2.5, using the height at 2 hours as the starting height. The candle was already 5 centimetres shorter by then.

Why C is wrong This is the burn rate in centimetres per hour, not a time.

Why D is wrong This divides 16.5 by 2.5, using the height at 5 hours and forgetting that 5 hours have already passed.

skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
stem_html:
\(3x+2y=34\)

\(5x-2y=14\)

What is the value of \(xy\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Opposite \(y\) coefficients invite addition.
  • Read what is asked. Three of the four choices are quantities you meet on the way.
  • Check both equations. \(5(6)-2(8)=14\).

Why A is wrong 8 is \(y\) alone.

Why B is right Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\): \(8x=48\), so \(x=6\). Substituting into the first gives \(18+2y=34\), so \(y=8\) and \(xy=48\).

Why C is wrong 14 is the right-hand side of the second equation, not a value of \(xy\).

Why D is wrong 6 is \(x\) alone. The question asks for the product.

skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
stem_html: A printer charges a \$40 setup fee plus \$3 per poster. A club has \$250 to spend. What is the greatest number of posters the club can order?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Set up the inequality before dividing.
  • An exact hit on the budget still counts.
  • Test the neighbours. 70 costs 250; 71 costs 253.

Why A is wrong 83 divides 250 by 3 and forgets the setup fee.

Why B is wrong 71 costs \(40+213=253\), which exceeds the budget.

Why C is right The condition is \(40+3n\le 250\), so \(3n\le 210\) and \(n\le 70\). Since 70 is a whole number and \(40+3(70)=250\) exactly, 70 posters is affordable.

Why D is wrong 69 rejects the boundary. The budget is met exactly at 70, and spending exactly \$250 is allowed.

stem_html: Line \(\ell\) passes through \((-2,\,9)\) and \((4,\,-3)\). What is the \(y\)-coordinate of the point where \(\ell\) crosses the \(y\)-axis?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Slope is rise over run, in that order.
  • The \(y\)-axis is \(x=0\).
  • Substitute back. At \(x=-2\), \(-2(-2)+5=9\).

Why A is wrong 3 comes from a slope of \(+2\), which reverses the sign of the rise.

Why B is wrong −2 is the slope, and it is also the \(x\)-coordinate of the first point. Neither is the intercept.

Why C is wrong 13 comes from \(9=-2(-2)+b\) solved as \(b=9+4\) instead of \(9-4\).

Why D is right The slope is \(\dfrac{-3-9}{4-(-2)}=\dfrac{-12}{6}=-2\). Using \((4,-3)\): \(-3=-2(4)+b\), so \(b=5\).

stem_html: A reservoir holds 5,400 cubic metres of water and is drawn down at a constant rate of 150 cubic metres per hour. Which function gives the volume \(V\), in cubic metres, remaining after \(t\) hours, for \(0\le t\le 36\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The starting amount is the constant term.
  • Draining makes the coefficient negative. Check the value at \(t=0\) and at \(t=36\).
  • 36 is an endpoint, not a rate. It is \(5400\div 150\).

Why A is right The reservoir starts at 5,400 cubic metres, so that is the constant term, and it loses 150 cubic metres for each hour, so the coefficient of \(t\) is \(-150\).

Why B is wrong A rate of loss subtracts. This function grows, reaching \(10{,}800\) at \(t=36\).

Why C is wrong This starts at \(-5400\), which is not a volume, and it is negative for the first 36 hours.

Why D is wrong 36 is the number of hours the reservoir lasts, not the rate. The rate is given in the question as 150.

stem_html:
\(\dfrac{2x+5}{3}-\dfrac{x-4}{2}=3\)

What is the solution to the given equation?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Clear the fractions on both sides. The 3 on the right becomes 18.
  • Watch the sign on the second numerator. \(-3(x-4)=-3x+12\).
  • Substitute back. \(\dfrac{-3}{3}-\dfrac{-8}{2}=-1+4=3\).

Why A is wrong −19 comes from multiplying only the left side by 6 and leaving the 3 alone: \(x+22=3\).

Why B is right Multiplying through by 6 gives \(2(2x+5)-3(x-4)=18\), so \(4x+10-3x+12=18\), which is \(x+22=18\) and \(x=-4\).

Why C is wrong 4 is the solution with the sign of the constant reversed; substituting 4 gives \(\dfrac{13}{3}-0=\dfrac{13}{3}\), not 3.

Why D is wrong 20 comes from distributing \(-3\) as \(-3x-12\): \(4x+10-3x-12=18\) gives \(x-2=18\). The minus sign applies to both terms, so \(-3(x-4)=-3x+12\).

stem_html:
\(x^{2}-10x+21=0\)

What is the sum of the solutions to the given equation?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Sum of roots is \(-b\); product is \(c\).
  • Factor when the numbers are small.
  • Read whether the sum, product or difference was asked for.

Why A is wrong −10 uses \(b\) itself instead of \(-b\).

Why B is wrong 4 is the difference \(7-3\).

Why C is right The equation factors as \((x-3)(x-7)=0\), so the solutions are 3 and 7 and their sum is 10. Equivalently, the sum of the roots of \(x^{2}+bx+c\) is \(-b\), which is 10.

Why D is wrong 21 is the product of the solutions, \(3\times 7\), not the sum.

stem_html: Which expression is equivalent to \(\dfrac{3x^{2}+5x-2}{9x^{2}-1}\) for all values of \(x\) at which both expressions are defined?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Factor both, then cancel. A difference of squares in the denominator is the way in: \(9x^{2}-1=(3x-1)(3x+1)\).
  • The shared factor is \(3x-1\), not \(3x+1\).
  • Expand your factorisation to check it.

Why A is wrong This cancels \(3x+1\) instead. The factor the two share is \(3x-1\): check by expanding \((3x-1)(x+2)\).

Why B is wrong The numerator factors with \(+2\), not \(-2\): \((3x-1)(x-2)=3x^{2}-7x+2\), which is not the numerator given.

Why C is wrong This is the reciprocal. The factor that cancels leaves the other factor of the numerator on top.

Why D is right The numerator factors as \((3x-1)(x+2)\) and the denominator as \((3x-1)(3x+1)\), so the common factor \(3x-1\) cancels and \(\dfrac{x+2}{3x+1}\) is left.

stem_html: The function \(p\) is defined by \(p(x)=3x^{2}+12x+7\). What is the minimum value of \(p\), and at what value of \(x\) does it occur?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "The minimum is \\(-5\\), at \\(x=-2\\)."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "The minimum is \\(-5\\), at \\(x=2\\).", "trap": "sign-flip"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "The minimum is \\(7\\), at \\(x=-2\\).", "trap": "solved-wrong-quantity"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "The minimum is \\(-2\\), at \\(x=-5\\).", "trap": "slope-intercept-swap"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • \(a\) is 3, not 1. The vertex formula divides by \(2a\), which is 6 here.
  • The constant term is \(p(0)\), and the vertex is not on the \(y\text{-axis}\).
  • Report the value and the input in the order asked.

Why A is right The vertex is at \(x=-\dfrac{b}{2a}=-\dfrac{12}{2(3)}=-2\), and \(p(-2)=3(4)-24+7=-5\). Since \(a=3>0\) the parabola opens upward, so this is a minimum.

Why B is wrong The sign of the vertex is reversed: \(-\dfrac{12}{6}=-2\), not \(2\).

Why C is wrong 7 is the constant term, which is \(p(0)\). The minimum is the value at the vertex.

Why D is wrong The two numbers are swapped. \(-2\) is the input and \(-5\) is the output.

stem_html: The function \(h(t)=45-2t^{2}\) gives the height, in metres, of a drone \(t\) seconds after it begins to descend, for \(0\le t\le 4\). At what height does the drone begin its descent, and what is its height when \(t=3\)?
choices_json: [{"letter":"A","content":"45 metres, then 18 metres","trap":"solved-wrong-quantity"},{"letter":"B","content":"45 metres, then 27 metres"},{"letter":"C","content":"45 metres, then 39 metres","trap":"shortcut-trap"},{"letter":"D","content":"2 metres, then 27 metres","trap":"axis-misread"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The exponent binds tighter than the coefficient. \(2t^{2}=2(t^{2})\), not \((2t)^{2}\).
  • The starting value is the constant term when \(t=0\).
  • Height, not distance fallen. The question asks where the drone is.

Why A is wrong This is the distance fallen, \(2(3)^{2}=18\), not the height. Subtract it from 45.

Why B is right The descent begins at \(t=0\), where \(h(0)=45\). At \(t=3\), \(h(3)=45-2(9)=45-18=27\).

Why C is wrong This computes \(45-2(3)=39\), forgetting the square altogether. The exponent applies to \(t\) before the coefficient multiplies.

Why D is wrong This reads the coefficient \(2\) as the starting height. The starting height is the constant, \(45\).

stem_html: Which expression is equivalent to \((3x-4)(2x+5)\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Four products, then combine.
  • Track the sign of each middle term separately.
  • Check at \(x=1\). \((-1)(7)=-7\) and \(6+7-20=-7\).

Why A is wrong The constant term is \((-4)(5)=-20\), which is negative.

Why B is wrong This multiplies only the first and last terms and drops the two middle products.

Why C is right The products are \(6x^{2}\), \(15x\), \(-8x\) and \(-20\), and \(15x-8x=7x\), giving \(6x^{2}+7x-20\).

Why D is wrong This takes \(8x-15x\) instead of \(15x-8x\).

stem_html:
\(\sqrt{3x+4}+2=x\)

What is the solution to the given equation?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Isolate the radical before squaring. Squaring \(\sqrt{3x+4}+2\) directly leaves a radical behind.
  • Squaring is not reversible. Every root has to go back into the original equation.
  • \(\sqrt{3x+4}=x-2\) forces \(x\ge 2\).

Why A is wrong \(x=0\) is the extraneous root. Substituting it gives \(\sqrt{4}+2=4\), which is not 0.

Why B is wrong Both roots of the squared equation are listed, but squaring can create solutions the original equation does not have. Each has to be checked.

Why C is wrong This is not a root of \(x^{2}-7x=0\) at all. The two roots are \(0\) and \(7\).

Why D is right Isolate the radical first: \(\sqrt{3x+4}=x-2\). Squaring gives \(3x+4=x^{2}-4x+4\), so \(x^{2}-7x=0\) and \(x(x-7)=0\), giving \(x=0\) and \(x=7\). Only \(x=7\) satisfies \(x\ge 2\), and \(\sqrt{25}+2=7\) while \(\sqrt{4}+2=4\ne 0\).

stem_html: A culture of bacteria doubles every 6 hours. If there are 500 cells at time \(t=0\), which function gives the number of cells after \(t\) hours?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The exponent counts periods. \(t\) hours is \(t/6\) doublings.
  • The base is the growth factor.
  • Test at \(t=6\). \(500\cdot 2^{1}=1000\).

Why A is right Each doubling multiplies the count by 2, and one doubling takes 6 hours, so the exponent counts doublings: \(t/6\).

Why B is wrong This doubles six times per hour, which is 36 times faster than described.

Why C is wrong This swaps the growth factor and the period; the culture multiplies by 2, not by 6.

Why D is wrong Growth by a constant factor is multiplicative, so the starting count multiplies rather than adds.

stem_html: A jacket is marked down 30%, and a member then takes a further 10% off the reduced price. The member pays \$126. What was the price before either reduction, in dollars?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Successive discounts multiply. 30% then 10% is not 40%.
  • Work with the fraction paid, not the fraction saved.
  • Check forward. \(200\times 0.7=140\), and \(140\times 0.9=126\).

Why A is wrong 140 is \(\dfrac{126}{0.9}\), which removes only the member's 10% and leaves the 30% markdown in.

Why B is right The member pays \(0.9\times 0.7=0.63\) of the original price, so the original is \(\dfrac{126}{0.63}=200\).

Why C is wrong 180 divides by 0.7 only, applying the member discount to nothing.

Why D is wrong 210 treats the two reductions as a single 40% off, \(\dfrac{126}{0.6}\). Successive percentages multiply rather than add.

skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
stem_html: A recipe calls for 350 grams of flour for every 4 loaves. A bakery has 14 kilograms of flour and wants to bake as many loaves as it can. How many loaves can it bake?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Kilograms against grams. Convert before dividing.
  • 350 grams is four loaves, not one.
  • A count of whole loaves rounds down.

Why A is wrong This divides 14 by 350 grams without converting the kilograms, then rounds. The two quantities have to be in the same unit.

Why B is wrong This rounds up. \(14{,}000\div 87.5\) comes out exactly at 160, and a 161st loaf would need flour the bakery does not have.

Why C is right 14 kilograms is \(14{,}000\) grams, and each loaf needs \(350\div 4=87.5\) grams, so \(14{,}000\div 87.5=160\) loaves.

Why D is wrong This divides 14,000 by 350 and stops, which counts batches of four loaves rather than loaves. Multiply by 4.

skill: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
stem_html:
The list below gives the number of books read by each of 7 students.

3, 4, 4, 6, 9, 12, 39

Which statement about the mean and the median of this list is true?
choices_json: [{"letter":"A","content":"The median is greater than the mean.","trap":"mean-vs-median"},{"letter":"B","content":"The mean and the median are equal.","trap":"mean-vs-median"},{"letter":"C","content":"The median is 9.","trap":"mean-vs-median"},{"letter":"D","content":"The mean is greater than the median."}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The median is the middle position, not the middle value of the range.
  • An outlier moves the mean and not the median.
  • Count the position: \(\dfrac{7+1}{2}=4\).

Why A is wrong A single large value, 39, pulls the mean up but leaves the middle value where it is.

Why B is wrong They are 11 and 6.

Why C is wrong 9 is the fifth value. With 7 values the median is the fourth.

Why D is right The sum is 77, so the mean is \(\dfrac{77}{7}=11\). The list is already in order and has 7 values, so the median is the fourth, which is 6. Since \(11>6\), the mean is greater.

stem_html:
The table shows the results of a survey of 200 people.

Owns a bicycleDoes not own a bicycleTotal
Under 30542680
30 or over3684120
Total90110200

If one of the people who own a bicycle is selected at random, what is the probability that the person is under 30?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The group selected from is the denominator.
  • “Of the people who…” names that group.
  • Both other totals appear as distractors.

Why A is right The selection is made from bicycle owners, so the denominator is the 90 owners and the numerator is the 54 owners under 30.

Why B is wrong 80 is the number of people under 30, which would be the denominator if the selection were made from that group instead.

Why C is wrong 200 is the whole survey, which is the denominator only for an unconditional probability.

Why D is wrong This is the probability that a person chosen from the whole survey owns a bicycle.

stem_html: In a town, 45% of the 3,600 registered voters voted in an election. Of those who voted, 60% voted for the incumbent. How many registered voters voted for the incumbent?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Two percentages in sequence, each on its own base.
  • The second base is the result of the first step.
  • Percentages of different wholes never add.

Why A is wrong 1,890 is \(52.5\%\) of 3,600, the average of the two percentages applied once to the whole register. The two act in sequence on different bases.

Why B is right \(0.45\times 3600=1620\) people voted, and \(0.60\times 1620=972\) of them voted for the incumbent.

Why C is wrong 1,620 is the number who voted, before the second percentage is applied.

Why D is wrong 2,160 applies 60% to all 3,600 registered voters rather than to those who voted.

stem_html: A line of best fit for a scatterplot of a car's age \(x\), in years, and its value \(y\), in dollars, is \(y=24{,}000-1{,}800x\). Which statement is the best interpretation of 1,800 in this model?
choices_json: [{"letter":"A","content":"The estimated age of the car when its value reaches zero.","trap":"solved-wrong-quantity"},{"letter":"B","content":"The estimated increase in the car's value for each additional year of age.","trap":"sign-flip"},{"letter":"C","content":"The estimated decrease in the car's value for each additional year of age."},{"letter":"D","content":"The estimated value of the car when it is new.","trap":"slope-intercept-swap"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The coefficient of \(x\) is a rate of change.
  • The constant term is the value at \(x=0\).
  • Carry the minus sign into the wording.

Why A is wrong That age is \(\dfrac{24000}{1800}\approx 13.3\) years, not 1,800.

Why B is wrong The coefficient is negative, so the value falls.

Why C is right 1,800 is the coefficient of \(x\), so it is the change in \(y\) per one-year increase in \(x\), and the minus sign makes that change a decrease.

Why D is wrong The value when new is the intercept, 24,000.

skill: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
stem_html: A data set of 8 values has a mean of 15. When a ninth value is added, the mean of the 9 values is 16. What is the ninth value?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Convert each mean into a total.
  • The new value is the difference of the totals.
  • Raising a mean by 1 across 9 values costs 9, plus the value's own share.

Why A is wrong 16 is the new mean. A value equal to the new mean would leave the mean unchanged only if it equalled the old one.

Why B is wrong 17 comes from adding the difference in means to the old mean, which ignores that the increase has to be supplied for all nine values.

Why C is wrong 31 comes from \(9\times 16-8\times 16\) plus 15, mixing the two totals.

Why D is right The first 8 values total \(8\times 15=120\), and the 9 values total \(9\times 16=144\). The ninth value is \(144-120=24\).

stem_html: In triangle \(ABC\), the measure of angle \(A\) is \(42^{\circ}\) and the measure of angle \(B\) is \(73^{\circ}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of the exterior angle at \(C\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Exterior angle equals the two remote interior angles.
  • Interior and exterior at the same vertex are supplementary.
  • Check: \(65+115=180\).

Why A is right The exterior angle at a vertex equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: \(42+73=115\).

Why B is wrong 65 is the interior angle at \(C\), \(180-115\).

Why C is wrong 138 is the exterior angle at \(A\), \(180-42\).

Why D is wrong 107 is \(180-73\), the exterior angle at \(B\).

stem_html: In right triangle \(XYZ\), the right angle is at \(Y\), \(XZ=17\), and \(YZ=8\). What is the value of \(\tan Z\)?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle. Here that is \(XZ\), not the longer leg.
  • Tangent never uses the hypotenuse.
  • Opposite over adjacent, measured from the named angle.

Why A is wrong This is \(\cos Z\), again using the hypotenuse.

Why B is right \(XZ\) is the hypotenuse, so \(XY=\sqrt{17^{2}-8^{2}}=\sqrt{289-64}=15\). From \(Z\), the opposite side is \(XY=15\) and the adjacent side is \(YZ=8\), so \(\tan Z=\dfrac{15}{8}\).

Why C is wrong This is \(\dfrac{1}{\tan Z}\), the adjacent over the opposite. Tangent is opposite over adjacent.

Why D is wrong This is \(\sin Z\). The hypotenuse belongs to sine and cosine, never to tangent.

stem_html: A circle in the \(xy\)-plane has equation \((x-5)^{2}+(y+2)^{2}=49\). What is the length of the circle's diameter?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The constant is \(r^{2}\), not \(r\).
  • Take the square root before doubling.
  • Read whether the radius or the diameter was asked for.

Why A is wrong 49 is \(r^{2}\), which is neither length.

Why B is wrong 98 doubles \(r^{2}\) instead of doubling \(r\).

Why C is right The right-hand side is \(r^{2}\), so \(r=7\) and the diameter is \(2r=14\).

Why D is wrong 7 is the radius. The question asks for the diameter.

stem_html: A right circular cylinder has radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. A second cylinder has the same height and twice the radius. How many times the volume of the first cylinder is the volume of the second?
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The radius is squared in the volume formula.
  • Only the scaled dimensions contribute a factor.
  • Check with numbers. \(640\pi\div 160\pi=4\).

Why A is wrong 2 is the factor by which the radius grew, not the volume.

Why B is wrong 8 would be the factor if all three dimensions scaled, but the height is unchanged.

Why C is wrong 6 adds the factors instead of applying the square.

Why D is right Volume is \(\pi r^{2}h\), so doubling \(r\) multiplies the volume by \(2^{2}=4\) when \(h\) is unchanged. Explicitly, \(\pi(4)^{2}(10)=160\pi\) and \(\pi(8)^{2}(10)=640\pi\).
